brief:
# Pressure Type

## Exact assigned author brief
“giant word PRESS is compressed by two plates then springs into generous letter spacing, sharp black/ivory with single acid accent.”

## Creative contract
The type behaves like a resilient material in a press. Inter Semibold is the object itself. Hard-edged black plates and their acid contact faces give the force a visible source. An ivory field keeps the black silhouette dominant. The strongest frame is the broad, released word at 7s, with the acid pressure trace below it. All shapes are authored vectors; the only asset is the bundled OFL Inter font.

## Beats
- 0–1.3s: plates approach slowly, the word makes first contact.
- 1.3–3.5s: pressure narrows and elongates the letterforms.
- 3.5–4.25s: loaded hold reveals the extreme compression.
- 4.25–6.8s: the pressure releases with a damped spring and individual letter overlap.
- 6.8–10s: plates withdraw; generous letter spacing holds the payoff.

## Failures to prevent
Plate/letter intersections that obscure reading; compression without contact; an unrelated slogan; clipping the released word.

## Editable controls
`scene.js`: C palette, pressure() load/rebound curve, word and spacing, plate() geometry. `index.html` owns font loading and fixed 1920×1080 drawing dimensions. The clock is window.seek(seconds).
review:

Renderer passed repeated and backward seek checks at four times. Repair: at 3.5s the first proof left about 90px between the squeezed word and each plate. Reduced the plate travel endpoints so the acid faces make visible contact with the loaded word. Re-rendered the proof.

brief:
# Chromatic Weave

## Exact author brief
Wide colored ribbons weave over and under; a traveling wave unpicks and reforms the fabric in a saturated editorial flat graphic composition.

## Creative contract
A fabric of broad coral weft and cobalt warp twists under a traveling diagonal wave. The crossings alternate rigorously, while loose ends explain the construction. Crisp, untextured color makes the woven silhouette readable. The hero is an expansive tilted swatch with visible over/under crossings, centered on warm ivory. Motion belongs to the material: the crossing coordinates move together so the interlacing remains coherent.

## Beats
- 0–1.4s: quiet fabric with a slight static twist.
- 1.4–4.7s: a rising traveling wave bends and separates the ribbons.
- 4.7–7.3s: the wave travels out and the crossings reform.
- 7.3–10s: a smaller afterwave runs through the finished textile.

## Hero time
7.3s

## Failures to prevent
Unconnected crossing patches, muddy palette, gap flicker, ribbons that look like a flat checkerboard without loose ends.

## Editable controls
`scene.js` contains the geometry, palette, timeline, and deterministic `window.seek(seconds)`. `index.html` fixes a native 1920×1080 canvas. All geometry is original and local; no external assets are used.

brief:
# Slice Clock

## Exact author brief
Eccentric black and white radial sectors lock into a striking optical sun, hold, and break apart in a spare Swiss graphic composition.

## Creative contract
Twenty-four black blades use their own radial pivot to lock into a mathematically exact optical sun. A second offset ring of radial sectors counter-rotates inside it, making a nested eclipse at the moment of lock. The field is warm white and absolutely spare. No typography or labels distract from the changing circle silhouette. The strongest state is an exact central optical sun framed with generous negative space.

## Beats
- 0–2s: loose radial blades turn at individual offsets.
- 2–4.4s: blade offsets disappear in a staggered locking wave.
- 4.4–6.6s: concentric optical sun holds as the inner register turns one tooth.
- 6.6–9.4s: alternate blades slide outward and rotate into a fragmented corona.
- 9.4–10s: fragmented silhouette resolves.

## Hero time
5.8s

## Failures to prevent
Accidental gray anti-aliased moire, an unreadable spinning fan, excessive full-frame rotation, an added title card.

## Editable controls

brief:
# Ink Relay

## Exact author brief
Smooth ink-like blobs pass momentum, merge into one emblem, then split. Use high-contrast cobalt and cream with smooth vector geometry and no noise.

## Creative contract
Four liquid masses pass a visible impulse from left to right, then travel inward to form a single four-lobed cobalt emblem. Circular lobes are joined by tangent Bezier necks, preserving clean ink edges through every connection. A small cream diamond appears as the emblem stabilizes, giving the hero a memorable counterform. This is a compact, wordless mark animation with abundant cream negative space.

## Beats
- 0–3.4s: a single impulse passes between four separated masses.
- 3.4–5.3s: all four masses converge into a rounded emblem.
- 5.3–6.9s: the counterform opens and the finished emblem holds.
- 6.9–9.3s: necks stretch then detach into four descending/ascending masses.
- 9.3–10s: the split state settles.

## Hero time
6.2s

## Failures to prevent
Visible seams at blob connections, lumpy polygon contours, disconnected splatter, an arbitrary circle that never changes silhouette.

# Typographic Tunnel

The front reading plane remains steady while depth compresses to one luminous word, then opens toward the opposite side. Lime identifies a traveling interior plane inside the ivory corridor. Inter Semibold supplies the actual letter outlines; the text remains readable at the broad front opening. This is typography behaving as space rather than an entrance effect.

## Beats
- 0–2.8s: depth extends toward the upper right and an acid plane travels into the corridor.
- 2.8–4.8s: the corridor compresses to the front reading plane.
- 4.8–7.2s: depth opens toward the lower left, reversing the perspective.

brief:
# Orbit Score

## Exact author brief
Colored discs travel along a constructed track, collide and exchange paths to form a visual musical score. Build a graphic concert identity without explanatory labels.

## Creative contract
Seven colored discs travel a continuous five-line serpentine track, behaving like notes before a score has settled. Two approaching discs make contact and rebound, redistributing the rhythm across the long route. The other discs keep traveling through rounded turnarounds before every note lands in a deliberate score-like arrangement. Ivory, ink, vermilion, cobalt, and ochre create a concert-poster identity; the track is the only line work and there is no text.

## Beats
- 0–2.35s: colored notes travel while two discs approach head-on.
- 2.35–3.4s: contact causes squash and a brief recoil.
- 3.4–7.8s: notes change their route positions and organize across five staff lines.
- 7.8–10s: a tiny final settling impulse yields the complete score.

## Hero time
8.5s

## Failures to prevent
Discs leaving the constructed track, teleporting notes at a turnaround, line discontinuities, excessive decorative notation or labels.

## Editable controls
`scene.js`: at() maps distance to an exact track location, distance() maps a target note back to the route, ends sets the final score, C sets note colors, and window.seek(seconds) owns all state. `index.html` fixes the native 1920×1080 canvas. All geometry is local and authored.

title: Soft Landing
brief:
# Soft Landing

## Creative contract

A lavender capsule drops onto a cream platform, compresses, rebounds and settles while tiny companion spheres react.

Impression: a tactile sculpture whose changing physical state carries the story. Wordless, no typography. Materials and palette: lavender, warm cream, apricot. All geometry and the reflected studio environment are authored locally.

## Hero

2.45s: the capsule flattens broadly against the cream disk while the small spheres hop.

## Beats

0–0.8s: capsule hovers above the platform. 0.8–2.25s: accelerating drop with a small stretch. 2.25–2.68s: deep squash and release. 2.68–5.28s: two decreasing rebounds. 5.28–10s: a soft settling hold.

## Mechanism and controls

Piecewise ballistic arcs meet volume-preserving squash; the capsule center follows its deformed half-height to preserve exact platform contact. `CONTROL` in scene.js sets form and timing; stage.js supplies editable camera, lighting, materials and mesh helpers.

## Failure conditions

Bottom must touch the platform at every compression; capsule must stay in frame while airborne; landing and rebounds should have distinct scale.

## Delivery

10 seconds, native 1920×1080, 30fps. index.html loads local Three.js 0.186.0 from ../../shared. `window.seek(seconds)` reconstructs all visible state. No soundtrack was authored. Collection root renders the final MP4.
review:
# Proof review

Inspected the starting hover, impact, maximum compression and rebound at 0, 2.25, 2.45 and 3 seconds, plus completed deterministic proofs at 6 and 9.5 seconds. title: Orbital Rings
brief:
# Orbital Rings

## Creative contract

Three polished champagne gimbal rings unlock from a spherical enclosure, orbit a pearl with an emerald core, and reunite.

Impression: a tactile sculpture whose changing physical state carries the story. Wordless, no typography. Materials and palette: deep emerald, champagne metal, warm pearl. All geometry and the reflected studio environment are authored locally.

## Hero

6s: three polished loops describe separate planes around the small emerald-and-pearl center.

## Beats

0–1s: closed armillary sphere. 1–4.1s: rings separate along independent orbital paths. 4.1–7.3s: three planes orbit the pearl core. 7.3–9.8s: the ring centers reunite. 9.8–10s: closed enclosure settles.

## Mechanism and controls

Independent ring groups follow three orbital phases while a split pearl shell reveals the emerald inner sphere; the ring clasps travel with their own geometry. `CONTROL` in scene.js sets form and timing; stage.js supplies editable camera, lighting, materials and mesh helpers.

## Failure conditions

Rings must retain clear separate silhouettes; clasps must move with each ring; metallic reflections must preserve the champagne tone.

## Delivery

10 seconds, native 1920×1080, 30fps. index.html loads local Three.js 0.186.0 from ../../shared. `window.seek(seconds)` reconstructs all visible state. No soundtrack was authored. Collection root renders the final MP4.

No visual repair was needed after the successful serial proof.
